questions.q_en: Which of the following is the correct relationship?
questions.solution_en:
· According to Newton's Second Law of Motion: Force (F) = mass (m) X acceleration (a).

· This is a fundamental principle in physics.

· This relationship shows that the force acting on an object is directly proportional to its mass and the acceleration it experiences.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following equation of motion is correct?

I. v = (u/2) + at

II. s = 2ut + at2
questions.solution_en:
Equation of motion:

· v = u + at

· v2 = u2 + 2as

· s = ut + at2/2

Hence, neither I nor II is correct equation of motion.

· v2 = u2 + 2as

questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT an example of inertia at rest?
options_en: Falling down backward when a vehicle starts immediately
Falling down of dust particle while dusting a cloth
The detachment of leaves/fruits due to shaking
The sudden application of brakes in a vehicle
questions.solution_en:
Inertia at rest (also known as inertia of rest) is the tendency of an object to remain in its state of rest. Options a, b, and c are examples of inertia of rest.

Option d, The sudden application of brakes in a vehicle is an example of inertia of motion. When brakes are applied suddenly, the vehicle (and the lower part of the passengers' bodies in contact with it) comes to rest, but due to inertia of motion, the upper part of the passengers' bodies tends to continue moving forward.

Explanation of Other Options (Examples of Inertia of Rest):

• Falling down backward when a vehicle starts immediately: When a vehicle starts suddenly, the lower part of a passenger's body in contact with the vehicle moves forward, but the upper part, due to inertia of rest, tends to remain at rest, causing the passenger to fall backward.

• Falling down of dust particle while dusting a cloth: When a cloth (like a carpet) is beaten with a stick, the cloth is set into motion, but the dust particles, due to inertia of rest, tend to remain in their position of rest and thus get separated from the moving cloth.

• The detachment of leaves/fruits due to shaking: When a tree branch is shaken vigorously, the branch moves, but the leaves/fruits, due to inertia of rest, tend to remain at rest and thus get detached.

Further insights:

• Inertia is the property of matter by which it continues in its existing state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line, unless that state is changed by an external force.

• There are three types of inertia: inertia of rest, inertia of motion, and inertia of direction.

• Inertia of motion is the tendency of an object to remain in its state of uniform motion.

questions.q_en: Identify the INCORRECT pair regarding motion and their examples.
options_en: Translatory motion  -  A ball falling from a cliff
Periodic motion  -  Hands of a clock
Oscillatory motion  -  Earth moving around the Sun
Rotatory motion  -  Blades of a fan
questions.solution_en:
· Oscillatory motion involves back-and-forth movement (e.g., a pendulum).

· The Earth moving around the Sun follows an elliptical orbit, which is an example of circular motion rather than oscillatory motion.

questions.q_en: A bus moving on a straight road at a speed of 10 km/h increases its speed to 70 km/h in 2 minutes. Find its average acceleration.
questions.solution_en:
• Initial velocity = 10 km/h, final velocity = 70 km/h, time = 2 minutes.

• Acceleration = (Δv / Δt) = (70 - 10) km/h / 2 min = 60 km/h / 2 min.

• Convert units: 60 km/h = 60/60 km/min = 1 km/min.

• Acceleration = 1 km/min / 2 min = 0.5 km/min².

Further Insight:

• Acceleration measures the rate of velocity change, critical in motion analysis.

• Formula for average acceleration: Average acceleration (a) is given by the formula: a = (Δv / Δt).

• The unit conversion ensures consistency, as km/min² is appropriate given the time in minutes.

questions.q_en: A javelin thrown by an athlete is in ________ motion.
questions.solution_en: A javelin follows a curvilinear motion as it moves along a parabolic trajectory due to the combined effect of initial velocity and gravity.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is correct about uniform acceleration?
options_en: An object moving on friction-less surface can gain uniform acceleration.
An object under free fall is an example of uniform acceleration.
An object moving with constant speed is an example of uniform acceleration.
Motion of a spring is an example of uniform acceleration.
questions.solution_en: When an object is travelling in a straight line with an increase in velocity at equal intervals of time, then the object is said to be in uniform acceleration. Free falling of an object is an example of uniform acceleration.
questions.solution_hi: When an object is travelling in a straight line with an increase in velocity at equal intervals of time, then the object is said to be in uniform acceleration. Free falling of an object is an example of uniform acceleration.

questions.q_en: The motion of the body moving along a circular path is an example of _______.
questions.solution_en:
When a body moves in a circular path, it is said to be in a circular motion. An object moving in a circular path may have constant speed. While the speed of the object is constant, its velocity is changing.

When the velocity of the object changes, we say that the object is accelerating. The change in the velocity could be due to change in its magnitude or the direction of the motion or both.

For example, if the athlete moves with a velocity of constant magnitude along the circular path, the only change in his velocity is due to the change in the direction of motion. The motion of the athlete moving along a circular path is, therefore, an example of an accelerated motion.

questions.q_en: If the uncertainty in position and momentum are equal, the uncertainty in velocity will be:
questions.solution_en:
According to the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle:

Δx. Δp ≥ h/4π

Δx = Change in position

Δp = Change in momentum

Δp. Δp ≥ h/4π [uncertainty in position and momentum are equal]

(mΔv)2 ≥ h/4π

Δv2 ≥ 1/4m * h/π

Δv ≥ 1/2m√h/π

Hence, option (b) is correct.
